method.main: Current main/service/storage code bundled with only isolated provider adapter, dummy seed, hidden-window and explicit persistence fault hooks. Current production preload and renderer are reused.
method.credentials: Each disposable profile starts with a dummy original-account record encrypted by actual Electron safeStorage. Reports contain no password, token, ciphertext or raw account identifier.
fallbacks: Protected-storage availability is modeled unavailable at writeConnection after the original account has loaded, while native crypto remains available for seed/restart verification.
A damaged owned device-identity file exercises actual nonpersistent-identity fallback; a successful account replacement must clear the old protected record.
method.failure: A held clear observes the original account and byte-identical canonical file while the form is pending. An injected deletion failure rejects the replacement. A fresh process restores the original account before a new explicit attempt succeeds.
method.success: The new distinct account is session-only, old encrypted connection.enc is absent, the warning is visible, and actual replacement music decodes. On a fresh process with protected storage available, no account or authentication request returns.
method.isolation: Owned localhost catalog only, dummy encrypted credentials, no shared provider key access or non-local network; server terminated after completion.

checks.productionBuildTypeScriptAndFullLint: PR47 passed. Every recorded app/source/artifact hash still matches that snapshot; no application/configuration change, so not repeated.

limits: Availability and deletion failure are controlled fault conditions, not an actual macOS protected-store outage or locked-Keychain prompt. Encryption/decryption, protected-file retention/removal, native UI, decoded music and fresh-process restart use the actual OS.
One Mac/runtime and substituted Jellyfin account responses; no claim about arbitrary OS/server/permission combinations, hardware controls or observed listener clarity.
This proves session-only account replacement. Playlist-access coverage and live read-only permission configurations retain their separate requirements.
